newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan unaware of concrete Thai rescue plan - source.
newsitem.headline: Japan unaware of concrete Thai rescue plan - source.

text.p: Japan is not aware of any concrete rescue plan to help Thailand cope with a sharp fall in its foreign reserves, an international monetary source told reporters on Friday.
He added that the Thai finance minister plans to visit Japan next week and Japanese authorities are hoping to have an exchange of views with him.
He said, however, that, "I am not aware of any particular rescue package for Thailand."

Thai officials have said that the country would try to raise a total of $10 billion, consisting of $5 billion in loans from banks and $5 billion in bond issues, in order to replenish reserves that were severely depleted when it defended the baht against speculative attacks in May.

The source said that Japan initially wants to monitor Thai economic policies aimed at stabilisation of the baht, after Thailand's decision last week to float its currency and allow it to fluctuate in line with the country's economic fundamentals.
The source declined to comment about the possibility of Japan using a so-called Asian repo pact to assist Thailand.

In April of 1996, Japan agreed with the monetary authorities of Australia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand to establish bilateral repurchase agreements to provide liquidity in times of currency crises. South Korea joined the pact in January of this year.
The repo pact gives participants instant access to cash by selling their holdings of U.S. government securities to the pact's partners with a promise to buy them back later.

Asked if Japan would be willing to lend money to Thailand via the repo pact if Thailand made such a request, the source said this technically was possible, although the repo pact only offers short-term liquidity to any country.

Asked if the baht's woes could spread to the currencies of other emerging Asian economies, the source said that he was not worried about such a possibility because the fundamentals of those economies were basically sound.

He also said that Japan has so far not received any request from the Philippines for financial assistance in the wake of its decision on Friday to widen the band in which its currency can fluctuate against the dollar.
